title: The Debt of the DMZ
premise: Silas Okafor, a crash investigator who lost her family in the row-twelve disaster she was never allowed to officially investigate, has built a career on cases no agency wants to claim. When Flight 4471's records evaporate mid-flight and the plane lands carrying a dead whistleblower, she uncovers 'the Network'—a private intelligence firm that trains deniable operatives and erases its own casualties. As she follows the trail from Seoul to Frankfurt with a defected trainer named Marek Voss, Silas realizes her family's crash was the Network's first field test. In the climax, she burns their archive hours before markets open in Frankfurt, exposing the operation at the cost of her anonymity—and finally claiming the truth about row twelve.
about_author: Elodie Sterling is a former aviation insurance analyst who spent a decade reading accident reports most people never see. She writes thrillers from a farmhouse outside Gdansk, where she keeps a wall of unsolved flight numbers.

chapters.title: Row Twelve
chapters.summary: Silas Okafor opens a cold-case file she keeps hidden beneath her desk: the crash that killed her parents and sister in row twelve. POV Silas. Establishes her ritual of remembering what the record says never happened. Emotional beat: grief sharpened into professional detachment.

chapters.title: The Unattributed
chapters.summary: Silas takes a contract no one wants: a cargo incident in the Baltic that three governments have declined to own. Her handler warns her to keep it quiet. POV Silas. Emotional beat: the comfort of being invisible, and the first itch of suspicion that invisibility is assigned, not chosen.

chapters.title: Ghosts on the Manifest
chapters.summary: Cross-referencing passenger lists, Silas finds six names that appear on other 'unattributed' incidents—including one from her family's flight. POV Silas. Emotional beat: dread curdling into obsession as coincidence collapses into pattern.

chapters.title: Flight 4471
chapters.summary: A passenger jet over the Caspian goes dark on every tracking system while still airborne. Silas is called in because no one else will touch it. POV Silas. Emotional beat: adrenaline and vertigo—the case is live, not historical.

chapters.title: Erased Mid-Air
chapters.summary: The plane lands safely, but every record—flight plan, crew files, maintenance logs—has been purged within ninety minutes. Silas photographs what she can before the hangar is sealed. POV Silas. Emotional beat: fury at the efficiency of the erasure; someone practiced this.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Seated
chapters.summary: One body in the cargo hold doesn't match any manifest: a dead man with a burner phone sewn into his coat. POV Silas. Emotional beat: cold clarity—the victim wanted to be found by exactly one kind of person. Someone like her.

chapters.title: Marek
chapters.summary: The phone leads to Prague, where ex-Network trainer Marek Voss has been hiding for three years. He recognizes the kill protocol instantly. POV alternates Silas/Marek. Emotional beat: wary mutual recognition between two people shaped by the same machine.

chapters.title: The Training Ground
chapters.summary: Marek explains the Network: it recruits orphans of unattributed disasters, trains them as deniable assets, and retires them permanently. Silas realizes recruits are made from crashes like hers. POV Marek. Emotional beat: guilt—he trained some of them himself.

chapters.title: What the Archive Keeps
chapters.summary: Marek reveals the Network stores everything in a Frankfurt data vault tied to a financial clearinghouse; exposure must land before markets open Friday. POV Marek. Emotional beat: hope with a deadline attached.

chapters.title: Tail Number Silence
chapters.summary: Someone wipes Silas's own credentials; her apartment is searched but nothing taken—a message. She moves to a safehouse with Marek. POV Silas. Emotional beat: the hunter becomes visible; loneliness gives way to an uneasy partnership.

chapters.title: The Recruit Who Called Back
chapters.summary: A young asset named Imani contacts Silas, believing she's reaching a friendly analyst. She's the whistleblower's protégée and holds half his evidence. POV Imani. Emotional beat: found family forming in the margins of a manhunt.

chapters.title: Frankfurt Bound
chapters.summary: The trio travels separately to Frankfurt under cover identities Marek forged years ago. A Network cleaner tails Imani through the station. POV Imani. Emotional beat: terror and resolve; she chooses the team over self-preservation.

chapters.title: The Clearinghouse
chapters.summary: Silas scouts the vault's host building and discovers the Network's financial arm launders its operations through legitimate market infrastructure. POV Silas. Emotional beat: awe at how deep the rot runs—exposure means crashing markets, not just careers.

chapters.title: Loyalty Priced
chapters.summary: Marek's old student, Davor, offers him reinstatement if he delivers Silas. Marek stalls, lying to both sides. POV Marek. Emotional beat: loyalty vs. truth tearing him down the middle.

chapters.title: Imani Taken
chapters.summary: Davor's team grabs Imani and her drive. Silas wants to trade herself; Marek insists there's a third option. POV Silas. Emotional beat: love against duty—she'd burn the mission to save the girl.

chapters.title: The Exchange That Wasn't
chapters.summary: At the arranged handoff, Silas springs Marek's counter-plan: a decoy drive seeded with traceable malware. They recover Imani wounded but alive. POV Silas. Emotional beat: fierce relief hardening into commitment—no more running.

chapters.title: Ninety Minutes
chapters.summary: With dawn approaching and Frankfurt markets opening in ninety minutes, the trio infiltrates the vault through the loading bay during a shift change. POV alternating trio. Emotional beat: ticking-clock compression; every small failure now fatal.

chapters.title: The Vault
chapters.summary: Inside, Silas finds the master index—and her family's flight listed as 'Field Test One.' Davor confronts them; Marek talks him down with the truth he trained out of him. POV Silas. Emotional beat: devastating confirmation; grief becomes weaponized purpose.

chapters.title: Burn Protocol
chapters.summary: They seed the archive across every exchange feed simultaneously so deletion is impossible. Alarms trigger; Davor holds the corridor, buying them minutes. POV Marek. Emotional beat: sacrifice offered freely—loyalty finally pointed at truth.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: As Frankfurt opens, the Network's records cascade onto screens worldwide; its financial web seizes and collapses. Davor is arrested covering their exit. POV Silas. Emotional beat: catharsis—the invisible made undeniable.

chapters.title: Attribution
chapters.summary: Weeks later, official inquiries reopen the old crashes, including row twelve. Silas testifies under her real name for the first time, refusing protection. POV Silas. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into public truth; visibility embraced.

chapters.title: The Debt Repaid
chapters.summary: On the anniversary, Silas, Marek, and recovering Imani visit the memorial together—an improvised family bound by what they survived and exposed. A new unattributed file arrives; Silas smiles and opens it. POV Silas. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace, and the promise that the work continues.
